greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Peace be with you, gathered as one family in the presence of our Lord.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you wept over the city of Jerusalem: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the Lamb who was slain for our salvation: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you offer us the peace that the world cannot give: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The Lamb has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God.
homily:
Imagine, if you will, the weight of a sealed scroll. It is an image of everything we do not understand, everything that remains locked away from our sight. In the Book of Revelation, the scroll in the right hand of the One on the throne is heavy with the mysteries of history, the secrets of suffering, and the hidden purposes of God. John, the visionary, weeps. He weeps because no one is found worthy to open it. He weeps because the silence of heaven seems absolute. He weeps because, like any of us standing before the closed doors of our own lives, he wants to know what lies beneath the seals. He wants to know the 'why' of it all. He wants to see the map of the future.

I want you to hold onto this image: the scroll. Think of the way Benjamin Vo lived his life—a boy who was always looking for the code, always seeking the logic behind the system. Whether he was diving into the architecture of cloud infrastructure or simply watching the way a Boeing 737 moved through the air, Benjamin was a boy who wanted to see how things worked. He was a boy of brilliant curiosity. He understood that there was a design to the world, a structure waiting to be explored. And yet, we all come to moments where the scroll is sealed tight. We come to moments where the logic of the world fails us, where the math doesn't add up, and where the silence of God feels like a locked door. We stand there, like John, and we feel the ache of not knowing. We feel the ache of the unanswered question.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been five months since he went home to God. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile, the way he would share his thoughts about his 'con chim airlines'—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s suffering. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus draws near to Jerusalem, and he sees the city, and he weeps. He weeps because the people do not recognize the time of their visitation. He weeps because they are blind to the peace that is standing right in front of them. This is the hinge of the mystery. We often think that God is hidden, that he is behind the sealed scroll, that he is waiting in some distant heaven. But Jesus shows us that God is the one who walks the streets with us. God is the one who stands in our midst. And in the Book of Revelation, John is told, 'Do not weep. The lion of the tribe of Judah... has triumphed.' And what does he see? He sees a Lamb that seems to have been slain. The power of God is not found in the breaking of the seals by force; it is found in the Lamb who was slain, the one who gave everything, the one who entered into the suffering of the world to redeem it from within. Benjamin, in his own way, understood this. He was a boy who was willing to offer his own 'piggy bank'—his own security—for the sake of his uncle. He was a boy who understood that love is not about keeping; it is about giving. That is the logic of the Kingdom. That is the code that truly matters.

Consider the image of the Lamb again. He has seven horns and seven eyes—the fullness of power and the fullness of vision. He is the one who opens the scroll. He is the one who makes sense of the suffering. He is the one who holds Benjamin now in the Banquet of Heaven. Benjamin is not a mystery left unsolved; he is a life that has been fully gathered into the heart of the Lamb. He is fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced. He is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where Ben and his dad stood outside room 419, and Ben said with that earnest voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The Lamb who was slain is the Lamb who is risen, and he is the one who promises that one day, every tear will be wiped away, and every scroll will be opened, and we will see clearly that love was the only thing that ever mattered.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of his face shine upon you forever. Go in the peace of Christ.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ.
For all who carry the heavy cross of grief, that they may be consoled by the presence of the Holy Spirit and filled with the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, saw a scroll in the right hand of the one who sat on the throne.
It had writing on both sides and was sealed with seven seals.
Then I saw a mighty angel who proclaimed in a loud voice,
“Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?”
But no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth
was able to open the scroll or to examine it.
I shed many tears because no one was found worthy
to open the scroll or to examine it.
One of the elders said to me, “Do not weep.
The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has triumphed,
enabling him to open the scroll with its seven seals.”Then I saw standing in the midst of the throne
and the four living creatures and the elders
a Lamb that seemed to have been slain.
He had seven horns and seven eyes;
these are the seven spirits of God sent out into the whole world.
He came and received the scroll from the right hand
of the one who sat on the throne.
When he took it,
the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders
fell down before the Lamb.
Each of the elders held a harp and gold bowls filled with incense,
which are the prayers of the holy ones.
They sang a new hymn:“Worthy are you to receive the scroll
and break open its seals,
for you were slain and with your Blood you purchased for God
those from every tribe and tongue, people and nation.
You made them a kingdom and priests for our God,
and they will reign on earth.”

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (Rev. 5:10) The Lamb has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Sing to the LORD a new song
of praise in the assembly of the faithful.
Let Israel be glad in their maker,
let the children of Zion rejoice in their king.
R. The Lamb has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Let them praise his name in the festive dance,
let them sing praise to him with timbrel and harp.
For the LORD loves his people,
and he adorns the lowly with victory.
R. The Lamb has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Let the faithful exult in glory;
let them sing for joy upon their couches;
Let the high praises of God be in their throats.
This is the glory of all his faithful. Alleluia.
R. The Lamb has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God.
or:
R. Alleluia.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
As Jesus drew near Jerusalem,
he saw the city and wept over it, saying,
“If this day you only knew what makes for peace–
but now it is hidden from your eyes.
For the days are coming upon you
when your enemies will raise a palisade against you;
they will encircle you and hem you in on all sides.
They will smash you to the ground and your children within you,
and they will not leave one stone upon another within you
because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
